newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Yiu Wing in share swap with China firm.
newsitem.headline: Yiu Wing in share swap with China firm.

text.p: Yiu Wing International Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday it will acquire a 40 percent stake in Chinese power firm Hubei Changzhou Power Development Co Ltd from China Chang Jiang Energy Corp.
In return, the Hong Kong company will transfer its 48 percent stake in Chinese equipment maker Wuhan Changfa Electric Power Equipment to Chang Jiang, Yiu Wing said in a statement.

The invested capital of the Changfa shares to be swapped, and the combined value of the invested capital and shareholders' loans of the Changzhou shares in question, were both worth 81.6 million, the statement said.
But an independent appraisal report put the value of the 40 percent stake in Changzhou at 175 million yuan, it said.
Yiu Wing is engaged in building construction and maintenance, property investment and development, restaurant operations and other investment activities.

On completion of the transactions, Yiu Wing will hold 40 percent of Changzhou, Chang Jiang will hold 20 percent and Sun Hung Kai Securities Ltd, a unit of Sun Hung Kai & Co Ltd, will retain its 40 percent stake.
Yiu Wing chairman Cheung Yiu-wing said the company's move was aimed at acquiring a more steady income source as the local government had agreed to buy all power generated by Changzhou.
The Hong Kong firm will reap from Changzhou an annual income of 20 million to 30 million yuan, representing a return on investment of 16 to 18 percent, he said.
The Hong Kong company is expected to recoup its investment in Changzhou in six to seven years, the statement said.
Changzhou is now on trial run and will be fully operational in July. Its joint venture period has been extended to 25 years from the original 15 years.
